title: field-voices-digest-and-execution-cribsheet-2026-04-30
content:
TL;DR:
- Quick synthesis of field conversations (Apr 15–29) focused on latency spikes, cache misses, and opaque error cases when customers scale bursts.
- This doc is an execution-first cribsheet: distilled asks, short-term patches, and a recommended next-steps cadence for Eng/Platform/Support.

Customer vignettes (short)
1) FinSearch (enterprise): observed 2–3% error rate under 500rps bursts; complaint: 'fallthrough to 1.5x-latency model variant without clear signal'. Wants explicit fallback logs + per-request reason code.
2) HealthAI (regulated): needs private deployment KV-cache eviction visibility; saw regressions after model pin update. Asks: 'how do we know what cache entries were invalidated when we roll?'.
3) ChatOps startup (PLG): cost-sensitive, uses Redwood-hosted API. Primary ask: cheaper short-token completions—suggestions to apply micro-batching at 8 tokens or offer a low-cost t2 variant.

Patterns & hypotheses
- Pattern A: bursts (10–20s) cause cache misses -> backend route to cheaper CPU-backed fallback or higher-latency model variant. Customers don't want silent fallbacks.
- Pattern B: rollout pinning + model quantization changes sometimes invalidate prefix caches; customers lack visibility into cache invalidation events.
- Pattern C: small-text-heavy workloads are sensitive to batching thresholds (default batch windows cause waste).

Immediate (0–2 week) microfix candidates
- Add 'fallback_reason' field to API response header when model routing changes (low-risk, UI + SDK update). Effort: small. Owners: API + SDK teams. Links: JIRA-4321.
- Expose cache-invalidation webhook for Dedicated & Private (opt-in) that emits TTL/resync events for pinned model rollouts. Effort: medium. Owners: serving-runtime + private-deployments.
- Short-token microbatch flag: server-side opt-in to reduce batch window for <=12-token requests. Effort: small. Owners: serving-runtime.

Priority mapping (triage)
- P0: Transparent fallback signals (customer-facing) + docs (FinSearch, HealthAI) — impact: high, effort: small-medium.
- P1: Cache-invalidation webhook + rollout audit logs — impact: high for enterprise, effort: medium.
- P2: Microbatch short-token optimization — impact: medium, effort: small.

Engineering notes / constraints
- Serving runtime: adding header + reason codes is straightforward but needs standardization across Dedicated/private hood. Watch SLA metrics for header emission rate.
- KV cache: the cache key namespace is per-model + pin id. Rollouts sometimes change pin; to produce meaningful webhooks we must capture pin changes at control plane.
- Batching: microbatching reduces cost but may add jitter. Provide observable toggles and safety limits (min throughput thresholds).

Customer-support playbook (short)
- When customer reports 'silent higher latency variant': patch-support template (copy/paste): ask for example request_id(s), timestamps, route_id, and model pin. If available, check rollout audit for same time window; if not, escalate to runtime team with 'fallback_reason' flag request.
- For cache anomalies: request last two rollout events and the pin mapping. Offer to enable temporary increased cache TTL as temporary mitigation.

Open questions / undecided
- Should fallback_reason be string tokens or numeric codes? (Prefer: codes + mapping table in docs).
- Do we ship cache webhooks only to Dedicated & Private or also hosted customers (opt-in)? Compliance concerns for hosted customers need review.
- Cost model: microbatching for short tokens — do we bill differently or preserve existing unit pricing? Product needs to decide on billing signal.

Mini experiment plan (2-week spike)
- Week 1: implement response header + mapping table (runtime + SDKs). Deploy to canary cluster. Run synthetic burst tests replicating FinSearch pattern.
- Week 2: enable short-token microbatch flag behind feature toggle for a small set of routes; monitor median P99, cost per token, and customer QoE.

Action owners & next steps
- API/SDK: Omar Patel — define header schema and SDK exposure (due: 2026-05-07).
- Serving runtime: Samir Gupta — implement microbatch flag + fallback_reason emission (due: 2026-05-14).
- Private deployments: Lena Rodriguez — design cache invalidation webhook payload and opt-in flow (due: 2026-05-21).
- CS owners: Maya Chen — run partner outreach to FinSearch + HealthAI with a short survey and invite to pilot (by 2026-05-05).

Notes to self / collateral ideas (quick)
- Create a short one-pager for Sales: 'How Redwood surfaces routing fallbacks' (focus on observability).
- Template PR: 'Add fallback_reason to response headers' with examples for Go/Node/Python snippets.

Meeting log (Apr 29, 2026)
Attendees: Maya, Omar, Samir, Lena, FinSearch eng lead (remote)
Key points: FinSearch sees cold-start perceived as regression; wants per-request telemetry. Agreed: start with header + docs and run a joint debugging session.

Fragmented raw quotes (as said on calls)
- 'We couldn't tell why the model changed — it just got slow.' — FinSearch eng lead
- 'We rolled a pin and things felt different; no visibility on cache.' — HealthAI infra
- 'Small completions are the bread and butter; batching killed our margin.' — ChatOps founder

Appendix (small)
- Quick checklist for implementing header: name, allowed values, SDK mapping, versioning rules, privacy considerations.
- Suggested doc page: /docs/platform/fallbacks-and-observability (draft).

Unresolved followups
- Product: decide on billing treatment for batch-mode optimizations.
- Legal: check hosted opt-in telemetry for PII leakage (for webhook schema).

---
End of cribsheet. Short, execution-oriented; use for sprint-0 planning and CS->Eng handoff.
